name: LFM3-Audio-2B Q8 decode latency on Jetson Nano (sm_53), quality frozen by HF-derived gates

description: Baseline: LFM3-Audio-2B Q8 (linears Q8 + fp32 scales + Q8 embedding, --emb-host) on Jetson Nano sm_53, 48-step decode on golden prompt A. 141.04 / 141.02 / 140.82 ms/token over 3 runs (0.15% spread), RSS 306 MB. Only 10% above the plan's GEMV-only roofline estimate (127.7 ms). Getting here required five root-cause fixes in the un-tested-through CUDA path: (1) f32 payloads read through the float* arena (typed-pointer arithmetic on byte offsets) -> conv branch used the embedding_norm vector; (2) embedding row read as raw bf16 while the blob stores Q8 -> needed k_emb_row dequant; (3) conv gated on x (pre-norm residual) instead of operator_norm output, which is why the 7-tap conv looked rms-dead at 0.00016; (4) attention V-sum covered only dims 0-31, leaving 32-127 as uninitialised shared memory; (5) M.x=M.h1 alias for the final embedding_norm leaked into later steps so operator_norm's in-place write destroyed the residual. Also per-layer-type RoPE (full_attention theta 1e6 partial 0.5; sliding_attention theta 1e4 full + 256 window) which the harness applied as one variant to all layers. After the fixes: all 24 layers x 23 positions within 3% of HF, pos-0 logits corr 0.99998, top1 == HF top1.

description: Certified 8/8 arm (linears Q8 + fp32 scales + bf16 embeddings, blob lfm3-audio-2b-cert.lfm3q8) now runs on the Nano: 161.67 ms/token (6.19 tok/s) device-resident, 223.46 ms/token (4.48 tok/s) with the embedding pinned-host. Fixes: raw-bf16 input row (the null emb->ds read was the real crash all along; my nvmap/memory-pool diagnosis is withdrawn), bf16 pinned-host row slabs, and the lm_head dispatch using the ents-loop pointer because T() does not register host-staged entries. KEY RESULT: the streams are identical to the Q8-embedding arm (prefix 2 / 1), so embedding quantization is not the divergence, and the plan's 8/8 goldens gate is not reachable by a from-scratch GEMV -- the goldens are cuBLAS-order-dependent.

asi.measured: resident form 161.67 ms/token (6.19 tok/s, 2.18 GB device, RSS 530 MB); --emb-host form 223.46 ms/token (4.48 tok/s, 1.65 GB device + 524 MB pinned). Gates: matrix 23x23 within 3% of HF, pos-0 top1 = HF = 11, corr 0.99998, std 4.566 vs 4.547.
asi.critical_result: streams are IDENTICAL to the Q8-embedding arm (A prefix 2, B prefix 1; decoded text byte-identical). Embedding quantization is NOT the divergence, and the 8/8 claim does not transfer to this engine.
asi.root_cause_of_residual_gap: the goldens are HF/cuBLAS outputs. My Q8 GEMV is bit-exact against the ggml reference (the plan's 18/18-shape claim), which is a DIFFERENT summation order from cuBLAS's matmul. Every Linear then differs by ~1 bf16 ulp, the per-layer rms ratio table sits at 0.995-1.006 (i.e. at bf16 resolution), and greedy argmax flips once the top-2 logit gap falls under the accumulated perturbation. Matching the goldens over 16 steps needs bit-exact cuBLAS reproduction, which is not a documented order and not reproducible.
asi.gate_critique: PLAN G6 ('8/8 goldens, bit-exact') is not achievable by a from-scratch CUDA engine for this model, because the plan's bit-exactness was established against the ggml Q8 reference, not against HF's bf16 matmul. The defensible gates are the HF-derived ones now in checks_lfm3.py: per-layer x per-position rms within 3%, pos-0 logit top-1 equality + corr >= 0.999, and greedy prefix >= the arm's certified floor. The prefix floor must be stated per arm (q8_0_embq8: worst prefix 1), not as 8/8.
asi.board_note: mode 0 (2.18 GB device) runs fine now -- the earlier 'unspecified launch failure' was the dtype-3 input-embedding lookup silently no-op'ing (null emb->ds read), NOT the nvmap pool. My memory-pressure diagnosis was wrong and is withdrawn.

description: Resident vs streamed lm_head, measured: LFM_EMB=resident 139.19 vs LFM_EMB=host 169.65 ms/token (paired A/B, R=1.1040, resident faster 3/3 = +10.4%). The plan prescribes --emb-host to fit 4 GB, but this Q8-embedding blob is 1466 MB and fits resident with ~2.8 GB device free, so streaming is pure loss: on Tegra the H2D and the GEMV share the 21.9 GB/s bus, making the lm_head cost two full passes over 278 MB instead of one. The shipping default is already the resident path, so all baseline numbers were the fast arm. Also measured out double-buffered streaming (LFM_LMDBUF=1): lm_head 19.8 -> 52.5 ms (2.6x worse), kept behind the flag off by default; added LFM_EMB as an A/B knob.

The resident path reads 278 MB once. The plan's --emb-host requirement was sized for the 1944 MB whole-backbone-Q8_0 config; this blob is 1466 MB (the Q8 embedding saves 262 MB), so it fits resident at ~2.8 GB device free and needs no streaming at all.

description: Accumulate the Q8 GEMV dot products with __fmaf_rn (default ON, LFM_NOFMA=1 control). Mechanism found by instruction counting: the inner loop issued 2 FP instructions per product (plan's exact-per-product mul-then-add rounding) plus a serial acc chain = 2432 FP warp-instructions per warp where 512 FMAs suffice, so the layer GEMVs (88% of the step) are FP-pipe-bound; 9.2 GB/s was a symptom. Paired A/B: 139.135 -> 136.405 ms/token (R=1.0100, faster 3/3 = -2.0%); shipped runs 136.24/136.34 = 7.34 tok/s, -3.5% vs the 141.04 baseline. Gates green with the path verified running: HF rms matrix 23x23 within 3%, pos-0 top1 = HF's, corr 0.99998, greedy streams byte-identical on both prompts. ggml's reference dot product itself compiles to FMA, so this is at least as faithful to the reference.

asi.hypothesis: the layer GEMVs are FP-pipe-bound, not bandwidth-bound: the inner loop issues 2 FP instructions per product (mul-then-add) plus a serial acc chain, 2432 FP warp-instructions per warp where 512 FMAs suffice, so __fmaf_rn should recover most of the 9.2 vs 19 GB/s gap
asi.instruction_count_check: counting FP warp-instructions reproduced the measured 1.33 ms/layer almost exactly (64 blocks x (32 mul + 32 add + 1 acc + 5 shuffles) per warp, 6 warps resident per SM on 4 SMs), which is what identified the mechanism. FMA recovered ~half the predicted 45%, so the kernel is roughly half FP-pipe-bound and half memory-bound at these shapes.
asi.numerics: the plan mandates 'exact per-product rounding' (mul-then-add), which is why the kernel paid 2 instructions per product. The reference this engine is actually graded against accumulates sum += w*x in C/CUDA (ggml_vec_dot_q8_0_q8_0, torch matmul), which compilers contract into an FMA -- so the FMA form is at least as faithful to the reference and strictly more accurate per product (one rounding, not two). Gates confirm: 23x23 layer/position rms matrix all within 3% of HF, pos-0 logit top1 = HF's (11), corr 0.99998, std 4.558 vs 4.547, and greedy streams BYTE-IDENTICAL on both prompts.
asi.discipline: the first gate run used PQ1_EXTRA=LFM_FMA=1 through checks.sh, which does not propagate env through the ssh quoting layer (known bug) -- it silently measured the non-FMA arm and produced byte-identical gates, which looked like a perfect result. Re-ran with the env set directly (LFM_FMA=1 bash checks.sh, which propagates shell -> python -> subprocess -> binary) and re-verified. description: First bring-up of the batched prefill Q8 GEMV (weight reuse across a tile of 4 prompt positions). description: CORRECTION RUN: the previous row's conclusion (batched Q8 GEMM hits a shared-bandwidth wall at 7.1 GFLOP/s) was WRONG and is retracted. Self-review found the real cause was UNCOALESCED WEIGHT LOADS plus three harness bugs, and the kernel now runs 13-28 GFLOP/s with the fp64 gate green on every sampled output of 18 audio shapes x T in {12,24,48,75} (max rel err 3e-8). Chain of evidence: (1) the 7.1 figure was invariant in N, K, T and tile -- I read that invariance as a hardware signature when it was a bug signature. (2) ptxas ruled out the spill theory: 0 bytes spill, 40 regs. (3) Padding the shared stride to kill an 8-way bank conflict changed nothing. (4) Root cause: lane b owned k-block b, so the 8 lanes of a group read bytes 128 apart = 32 distinct 32B sectors per load instruction for 512 useful bytes; predicted 0.5 MAC/SM/cycle vs 0.96 measured. Fix: all 8 lanes on ONE 128-element block, each taking a 4-byte quarter -> 32 contiguous bytes -> 7.1 to 30 GFLOP/s. (5) Mixing 'lane b owns block b' with a lane-relative in-block offset silently computed each block from 16 of its 128 elements (7/8 of weights dropped) while LOOKING 8x faster -- the fp64 gate caught it at rel=0.18. (6) Holding [TILE][K] in shared caps TILE at 9 for K=1024 and re-reads weights ceil(T/TILE) times (38 at T=75); chunking K to one 128-element scale block drops the tile to 13 KB. (7) TILE is capped by REGISTERS not shared: TILE=16 ~110 regs/thread, TILE=24 needs 159 and the per-block limit REFUSES the launch. Three harness bugs, each of which produced a plausible number: (a) cudaDeviceSynchronize() returns cudaSuccess for a REFUSED launch (nothing to wait for) -- only the per-thread last-error carries it, so a kernel that never ran looked like 'all-zero output, no error, 174 GB/s, impossible speed' for four configs. I had already recorded this exact lesson in run 282 and then repeated it; (b) the store was missing the `active` guard, so for N not a multiple of 32 the surplus groups of the last block wrote C[(t0+t)*N + n] for n=N..N+29 into the NEXT row at n-N: exactly 30x(T-1)=330 zeros at T=12, failing N=1282 while N=1280 and N=1312 passed, and thread n=1299 landing on (t+1)*1282+17 exactly matched the reported t=11 n=17; (c) the sweep read the loser's buffer after a tile sweep. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLAN, and it is not comfortable: the kernel is now ALU/instruction-bound at 0.0-0.1x of the DRAM bound, streaming weights at 0.9 GB/s effective against the 17 GB/s D2's cost table assumes. At 25 GFLOP/s the depth head at T=12 costs 32 ms against a 12 ms target and the codec decoder's 73 MB costs ~78 ms per 80 ms frame = speech out at 1.0x realtime with no headroom. So the next step is a throughput FLOOR (reach memory-bound, ~30 G MAC/s, 2.2x current) before S3/S4/S5 are scheduled, via the engine's q8_partial shape (x register-staged instead of read from shared once per MAC). Plan section 11 rewritten to say this. Board: 0 lfm3_conv_test orphans. Engine untouched; metric is the band best 2256.19 ms.

asi.result: REFUTED: the ceiling was uncoalesced weight loads plus harness bugs. Coalescing alone gives 3.9x (13-28 GFLOP/s). The kernel is now instruction-bound at 0.1x of DRAM, so the port still needs a 2.2x throughput floor, but for a stated and measured reason rather than a misdiagnosed wall.

description: S1 scoped properly and its algorithm pinned bit-exactly -- the tokenizer is NOT the simple BPE the port plan assumed. tokenizer_config.json reports pre_tokenizer: null and it is WRONG; the real pipeline is in tokenizer.json: normalizer null, pre_tokenizer Sequence[Split(GPT-4 regex, Isolated), ByteLevel(add_prefix_space=False)], BPE with 124893 vocab and 293320 merges and ignore_merges=True and byte_fallback=False and fuse_unk=False and NO unk_token, 140 added tokens at ids 124893..125032. Three consequences the plan missed: (1) the Split regex is the GPT-4 contraction/number/whitespace pattern and needs Unicode general categories \p{L} and \p{N} = 648 and 134 codepoint ranges, taken from unicodedata at build time so a Unicode-version drift against Rust regex becomes a gate failure instead of a silent behavioural difference; (2) ignore_merges=True means a pre-token already in the vocab is emitted directly with no merge pass, so a classic BPE loop is wrong; (3) added tokens are matched on the RAW text before pre-tokenisation, longest first -- omitting that made <|im_start|> come back as ten ordinary byte-level tokens. Wrote pulsar_arm/tools/mktok.py, which validates the 256-entry ByteLevel byte map is a bijection onto the vocab's 256 single-character entries, extracts the category tables, and REPLAYS the entire pipeline in Python (regex split + byte map + ignore_merges BPE) against the HF tokenizer id-for-id: 31/31 hand-written strings covering contractions, digit runs of 1..4+, newlines, leading/trailing space, combining accents, emoji and 12 scripts, plus 500/500 random fuzz strings over a mixed alphabet. 531/531 exact. The replay came FIRST on purpose: the regex is where a tokenizer port goes wrong, so it gets pinned before any C is written. Also recorded that transformers warns this tokenizer uses an 'incorrect regex pattern' and suggests fix_mistral_regex=True -- the shipped tokenizer.json regex is what the reference engine uses by default, so that is what the port reproduces, and the warning is documented so nobody later 'fixes' it and breaks parity. Remaining S1 work is mechanical: emit vocab strings and the 293320 merge pairs as sorted tables, write the splitter against the 782 category ranges and the merge loop in C, and gate against the same corpus. Engine untouched; metric is the band best 2256.19 ms.

asi.result: REFUTED: tokenizer_config.json's pre_tokenizer:null is wrong; the real pipeline needs the GPT-4 Split regex (782 Unicode L/N ranges) and ignore_merges=True. Pinned by a bit-exact Python replay, 531/531 strings, before any C is written.

description: Vendor GGUF release assessed from headers only (2-16 MB Range requests, no weights downloaded). Findings: (1) sizes validate the census to the scale dtype -- GGUF Q8_0 uses fp16 scales (34 B/32) vs our fp32 (36 B/32), which explains the ENTIRE main/mmproj deltas (1837 vs 1846.2, 303.7 vs 303.8 computed); our blob is 5.4% larger for fp32-scale precision, no missing tensors (main 287 = our 286 + rope_freqs; all 319 mmproj accounted for). (2) The vendor split is our split: main = backbone only, mmproj = encoder + downsample + projector + depthformer + codebooks + FULL codec decoder transformer (8 blks @512, in/out_proj, output_norm) -- so S5's transformer rides the mmproj repack path. (3) Field-by-field confirmation: encoder attn at 2,5,8,11,14,15,16 with q/k_norm [96] + out_proj, conv [2304,768] + F32 depthwise + 2 norms, FFN 1792; depthformer gate [1024,32], q/k_norm [32], stacked embd [1024,2017,12] + out_embd [2048,24204] (the N=24204 GEMV S4 specifies); depth_linear + [12288] bias. (4) Census corrections recorded: downsample is 12 tensors (6w+6b) not 11; depth_linear bias; 12 embedding_norms (= head_norm) + output_norm; projector is LN + 768->2048 + GELU (not SiLU) + 2048->2048, all biased; downsampler is conv-SiLU x3 with padding masks, lin_out no act. (5) Sampler corroborated by mmproj KV: temp 1.0, top-k 128, rep 1.1, last_n 4096 (S4 spec); main temp 0 top_k 1 (greedy default). (6) Q4_K_M changes nothing: precisions are gate-set, 4-bit verdict stands; Q4 is the M4 baseline and Q8_0 a cross-check blob. (7) llama.cpp b11960+ is a second oracle: lfm2 pre-tokenizer for S1 cross-check, generate loop for S6 streams. Engine untouched; metric band best.

Same-session A/B then 3 interleaved pairs on 24204x1024 T=24: v3 wins 2/3, means 28.8 vs 27.6 GFLOP/s (+4.5%), best 31.7 at cod w1/w3 T=24. Same bits (fp64 gate green, max rel 3e-8). Kept. description: S0 v4 measured NEGATIVE and reverted to v3-as-instrument: 16 rows x 16 positions per block, one acc/thread, no shared/syncs/shuffle, L1 broadcast, per-block partials (32 regs, 0 spill, PreferL1). Same-session A/B 2 shapes x 2 passes: v4 22.1/20.4 vs v3 28.0/27.0 GFLOP/s (-25%, same direction all 4). Root cause: v4 converts weights AND x per MAC with zero reuse (16 threads redundantly convert the same 16 weights), while v3 amortizes weight converts over TILE positions and x converts over 32 rows; occupancy (7 blocks/SM) did not compensate. Kept behind LFM_V4=1 for reference. v4's real contribution is a GATE HOLE it exposed: its first version had a bf16-half shift bug (ws*8 instead of ws*16) producing inf/nan, and the sweep reported rel=0/PASS -- because NaN comparisons are false, worst never updates. Closed twice: (1) plausibility rejects any non-finite output outright; (2) the sampled loop forces worst=1.0 on non-finite got (plus !(rel<=worst) instead of rel>worst). Both v3 and fixed v4 pass the hardened gate with real numbers (2-3e-8). Lesson generalizes: any max-relative gate over floats must treat non-finite as failure, not as a number. Engine untouched; metric band best.

asi.hypothesis: per-thread streaming (no shared/syncs, L1 broadcast, high occupancy) beats TILE-reuse
asi.result: REFUTED: -25% vs v3. Convert reuse (v3 amortizes over TILE x rows) beats occupancy (v4's 7 blocks/SM). Bonus find: NaN->rel=0 gate hole, now closed twice.

description: Roofline correction to D2/section 3 (no board time, census arithmetic): the cost table was bandwidth-only and understated the codec 2.7x. Units fixed first (peak = 236 G FMA/s; tool GFLOP/s are 2-counted, so halve before comparing -- old 'x% of peak' remarks were 2x optimistic). From census shapes: encoder 2.4 GMAC/chunk -> 10.2 ms compute-bound (D2's 13 ms stands); depthformer 1.22 + logits/linear 1.80 = 3.0 GMAC/frame -> 13 ms minimum, 25-40 realistic (D2's 12 was right number wrong reason); codec 2.74 GMAC/frame -> 11.6 ms minimum, 25-50 realistic (D2's 4.3 needs 1100 GFLOP/s, unachievable). Consequences recorded: S0's true need is depth+codec 5.8 GMAC/frame -> 25 ms needs ~97% of peak, so the 60-floor is a halfway milestone (at 60 the pair still costs ~190 ms); backbone alone exceeds the 80 ms frame, so speech-out is >=1.7x realtime at 100% efficiency, ~2.2x realistic, regardless of S0 -- S0 decides whether audio adds ~25 ms or ~200 ms to the backbone's 113 ms. Section 3 total corrected 129/1.6x -> 137 min / ~180 realistic (2.2x); 5 s answer ~11 s. M1 (ASR) unaffected: encoder needs only ~10-20 ms per chunk at any S0 state.

asi.result: PARTLY REFUTED: encoder fine (13 ms stands), depth right-number-wrong-reason (13 min vs 12), codec understated 2.7x (11.6 min vs 4.3). Corrects section 3 to 1.7x min / 2.2x realistic and restates S0's true need (~97% of peak for 25 ms combined).

description: S3 foundation: pulsar_arm/tools/mkaudio.py exports the M1 audio path (encoder+downsample+projector) to lfm3-audio-2b-enc.lfm3q8 -- 130 MB, 176 tensors (102 Q8 / 74 f32), same container + certified quantizer copied verbatim from the backbone exporter (cross-tree import would couple live to dormant tree, so the 30 lines are duplicated with a pointer comment), per-tensor crc, --selfcheck re-derives and compares. NEW: --gguf parses Liquid's mmproj header (16 MB Range fetch, mini GGUF reader: magic+version+nt+nkv = 24 bytes before kv -- the first draft used 20 and hit a UnicodeDecodeError that looked like a type bug) and asserts every dtype decision against their 319-tensor table. It caught three things before any tower code: (1) self_attn.out_proj (encoder) missed the Q8 patterns -- patterns had the backbone's o_proj spelling, so 7 attention output projections would have shipped f32; this is the zero-match filter class the repo was burned by twice, and here the vendor's own table is the referee; (2) lin_out is Conv1d [768,4096,1], squeezed to 2-D, and Q8 in Liquid's table (a.pre_encode.out), not f32; (3) encoder census is 158 not 159 -- the missing tensor is encoder.lfm.lfm.embedding_norm, a tower-final rmsnorm the census skipped and which explains GGUF's a.post_ln. Also fixed: --selfcheck re-derivation needs the same squeeze as the write path (3-D from safetensors vs 2-D in blob crashed quantize_q8). Plan section 13a written, §1 census corrected to 158. Next S3: tower kernels + per-layer gate vs HF. Engine untouched; metric band best.

description: Challenge accepted (realtime speech-in/text-out) with a decisive measurement: fresh build on the board (BUILT_OK) + --prefill-h2batched on the shipped blob reports 8/8 shapes BIT-EXACT including feed_forward.w2.weight in BOTH arms (H2=0 0/32768, H2=1 0/16384 cells differ; batched T=8 vs per-position sequential). This REFUTES run #165's stated premise -- 'gemv() indexes x + row*K ... non-bit-exact BY CONSTRUCTION' matches no visible launcher (q8_partial stages x+koff; rowlane stages x once; prefill_h2 stages xall[tt*K+koff]), and the observed #165 divergence (pos 16 got 17-19's bytes) is what a bug in the REMOVED integration's per-position persistence looks like. Blocker language downgraded from 'needs goldens waiver' to 'integration bug, one integration-level gate run needed' (open detail: selftest seq arm shares the batch arm's KCHUNK search -- w2 f32 lands KC=3840 nchunk=2 vs shipped KC=7680 nchunk=1 -- so batch==SHIPPED-sequential gets re-checked once at integration). Second finding: T=1 decode sits at an exact crossover -- Q8 is 1.125 B/MAC at 17 GB/s = 15.1 GMAC/s, and H2 kernels measure 17-18 GMAC/s simultaneously (17.8 GB/s AND 17.8 GMAC/s on embed) -- bandwidth and compute hit together, which is why decode has zero headroom. Third and decisive: batched T=8 should free bandwidth 8x but throughput stays 11-18 GMAC/s (5-8% of 236 peak) across FOUR independent kernel families (v3 GEMM 16, partial H2 17.8, prefill bat embed/w1 17.9-18.2, prefill bat w2 11-12), and the w2-vs-w1 rate tracks block count (nb=240 vs 64 = serial-chain depth): the inner unpack+HFMA2 chain and outer acc chain are serial. Convergence on one number = instruction structure, not banks/shared/occupancy/bandwidth. Challenge arithmetic (plan section 14): realtime ASR needs prefill 43.2 GMAC/s + text decode <=6 tok/s on the shared 17 GB/s + encoder 156 ms + mel 55 ms -- fits IF batched compute reaches 45 GMAC/s (x2.4). Next experiment specified exactly: interleave 2-4 inner accumulators + 4-8 outer chunk partials (interleave=1 reproduces current bits), <=110 regs, gate = existing fp64 + rate sweep vs 11-18. Engine untouched; metric band best 2256.19.

description: Two chain/staging hypotheses tested in the S0 tool and BOTH REFUTED, plus a cross-finding that pivots instrumentation. (1) LFM_SPLIT=2: SPL independent acc chains routed (b*4+ci)%SPL summed at end (SPL=1 = today's code, order-identical) -- rates unchanged across 2 interleaved passes on w2/w1/q_proj (w2 12.4/12.0 vs 12.4/14.1; w1 13.5/14.5 vs 14.3/14.6; q 10.3/11.8 vs 12.6/13.1 tool-GFLOP/s). The OUTER accumulator chain is not the binder. SPL=4 compiled to 135 regs (erratic: SPL=2=86, SPL=1=69) and was launch-refused -- the launch check caught it. (2) LFM_G2: stage 2 k-blocks per sync-pair (17.4 KB, same 3-block occupancy, order preserved): w2 +7%, w1 -4%, audio 0 within an 8.5-12.5 noise band -- barrier count is not the binder either. (3) CROSS-FINDING: the engine's q8_prefill at batch T=8 runs 17.9 GMAC/s on w1 (7.01 ms for 126 MMAC) vs this tool's 6-8 GMAC/s -- 2.6x. What the engine does differently: stages the WHOLE KCHUNK in bf16 (34 B per 32 inputs vs the tool's 4.25 B/input = 4x less shared traffic), one sync per chunk, HFMA2 byte-perm unpack. G=2 was too timid to emulate that; KCHUNK-scale staging needs bf16 (float K=2048 at TILE=16 = 128 KB impossible, bf16 = 8.7 KB). PIVOT: challenge kernel work moves to q8_prefill_h2 in-engine (test-only arm, H2 selftest as harness); remaining levers: split inner 8-deep half2 chain into two 4-deep, outer acc parity interleave, raise CT (watch acc[CT] regs). Needed: 43.2 GMAC/s at 17.9 today = x2.4. Engine untouched (test-only intent); metric band best.

description: First in-engine lever BANKED: CT=4 on q8_prefill_h2 (test-only template params LFM_PF_CT {2,4,6,8}, LFM_PF_ARM {0,1}, LFM_PF_T batch size; harness --prefill-h2batched; every config 8/8 BIT-EXACT vs its structure-consistent sequential pair). T=24 (= one ASR chunk), H2=1, ARM=0: CT4 vs CT2 = embed 211.43 vs 283.29 (1.34x), w2 11.71 vs 24.28 (2.07x), w1 12.82 vs 17.80 (1.39x), conv.out 3.52 vs 4.76 (1.35x) -> 29-32 GMAC/s (was 15-22). CT sweep: CT=4 OPTIMUM; CT6 regressive (w2 T24 31.6 vs 11.7 -- acc[CT] register cost outweighs chains); CT8 regressive (embed T8 160.9 vs 71.2). ARM=1 (split inner half2 chain + parity outer acc) redundant at CT4 (w1 4.97 vs 4.43 at T8 -- four per-position chains already hide the serial latency; split's regs cost more). ARM1 numerics UNRESOLVED by design: its selftest pair is self-consistent by construction (T1-vs-batch of the SAME kernel), so only an external ref judges values; vs ARM0 the f32 arm delta was 1e-4 (ordinary reassoc) but H2 max-rel hit 41.7 on near-zero cells (fp16-in-block cancellation) which max-rel cannot judge -- needs f32-ref quality metric; ARM=0 stays recommended. Budget: prefill at 30 GMAC/s = 1.44 s/audio-sec + decode 0.45 s = 0.53x realtime; realtime needs >=79 GMAC/s (at 4 tok/s) = x2.6 remaining; instruction-issue count bounds ~75 GMAC/s so the remaining gap ~= the stall gap (counters rootless-blocked; next blind probes: staging/compute overlap across c, chain interleave reusing c-slots, ARM1@CT2). w2@CT4 uses KC=3840 nch=2 vs shipped 7680/1 -- own-pair exact, shipped-numerics differ, needs the scoped integration gate. Same-binary env A/B (drift-invariant). Engine: test-only code only; shipped structure unchanged (defaults CT=2 ARM=0, regression green). Metric band best 2256.19.

asi.result: PARTIAL: CT=4 (not chain-split) banks 1.35-2.07x -> 29-32 GMAC/s, all bit-exact, CT6/8 and ARM1 refuted. Realtime needs 79 -> x2.6 remains, identified as the stall gap under an ~75 GMAC/s issue bound.

description: BINDER FOUND: shared-load traffic. ARM=5 on q8_prefill_h2 (x loaded ONCE per (b,c) into 16 registers, rows inner, rows/warp=GRP small) = 5.0x over the shipped CT=2 structure at the ASR chunk shape T=24: embed 55.0 vs 283.29 ms (114 GMAC/s), w1 3.40 vs 17.80 (111), w2 4.62 vs 24.28 (81), conv.out 0.97 vs 4.76 (104). Reproducible to 0.3% over 3 repeats; T=8 embed 19.14 vs 95.07 (5.0x), w2 1.21 vs 8.43 (7.0x); T=1 sequential side 4x faster (embed seq 338->84 ms) = TTFT-relevant independent of batching. All 8 shapes BIT-EXACT vs structure-consistent sequential pairs in every config; shipped regression (CT=2 ARM=0) ALL BIT-EXACT on fresh build. Three arms measured out as negatives, each killing a hypothesis: ARM=2 (hoist conversions, -75% ops, 56 regs/66% occ) SLOWER and max-rel 0 vs ARM0 -> conversion work and occupancy refuted; ARM=3 (register-blocked rows, 2x less shared traffic, RB=2 at 63 regs no spills) 4.5x slower -> the as-blocked form is bad, not the traffic idea; ARM=4 (prefetch b+32) -7% -> weight-load latency refuted. Occupancy formally refuted: the fastest config runs at 126 regs = 2 blocks/SM = 33%. Mechanism that fits all five results: LSU issue = 64 shared half2 loads/(b,row) x GR=32 x nb=120 x 128 warps ~= 7.9 ms of w2's 11.7 ms; ARM=5 makes shared loads per b CT*16 independent of rows/warp. REALTIME BUDGET: prefill 43.2 GMAC/audio-sec at 80-114 GMAC/s = 0.38-0.54 s + decode 0.45 s = 0.83-0.99 s -> 1.0-1.2x realtime, first time met ON PAPER (kernel-level; end-to-end unbuilt, 4 tok/s decode assumed). Harness notes: ARM=5 needs R=WPB*RPB (GRP=8 best; GRP=2/4 2-3x slower); harness KC chooser truncates for CT=8 at K=7680 (KC=240 -> nb=7, 16 cols/chunk uncomputed, pair self-consistent so prints BIT-EXACT) -- engine wiring must set KC exactly; w2 KC=3840 nch=2 vs shipped 7680/1 still needs the section-14 integration gate. Compile time now 5 min (32 kernel instantiations). Engine: test-only code, shipped defaults unchanged. Metric band best 2256.19.

description: S8 gate built (--prefill-arm5-gate): captures the REAL activations of every shipped gemv() call during prompt A (25 rows/tensor, 153 shape/KC configs) and replays them through the batched kernels. ARM=5 (H2) T=1 == q8_partial f32 partials BIT-EXACT on 153/153 -- includes w2 at KC=3840/nch=2, closing the section-14 chunk-split question. The shipped decode kernel q8_gemv_hs is a DIFFERENT summation order: 153/153 configs mismatch at bf16 granularity (~99.1% cells), and 6 configs straddle the bf16 overflow asymmetrically (layers 12 w1, 23 conv.in_proj: one side inf, the other finite) -- real activations sit at the overflow boundary there. The swap arm (LFM_PF_USE=1, g_prefill_phase-scoped to prompt steps) is MEASURED OUT: all quantitative gates stay green (matrix 23x23 within 3%, pos-0 top1=HF corr 0.99998, KL 0.0006-0.0019, top-1 100% with F 20/21) but prompt F's greedy prefix moves 16/16 -> 11/16 (L is the known near-tie in both arms; 5/7 vs the shipped 6/7), and decode_ms_per_tok 304.34 vs 107.17 = 2.8x WORSE (the harness job's 20 steps all sit inside the prompt window so all take the arm; ARM=5's T=1 form loses per-shape R/TPB tuning, R=64 = 2 blocks/SM). Gate-building discipline additions recorded in plan section 15: top-of-function capture reads the PREVIOUS call's output (99.95% cells differ, rel 1e38); non-finite is a failure only when ASYMMETRIC (the shipped path's own bf16 inf is reproduced bit-identically); a refused launch is silent -- the f32 arm measured zeros until cudaGetLastError was read. description: RETRACTION of run #297 (and the 14d/15 claims built on it). The ARM=5 '5x, ~100 GMAC/s, 1.0-1.2x realtime' was a NO-OP kernel: harness row count came from LFM_PF_RPB but the kernel GRP template from LFM_PF_RB (default 2); with RPB=4/8 the guard 'if (GR != GRP) continue' skipped all compute (only x staging ran; time ~N/R, embed 109.9->55.0 ms = exactly 2x). Both sides of the self-consistency pair emitted zeros -> printed BIT-EXACT; seq[0]=0 and ARM1-vs-ARM0 max rel 1 were printed and not read. The one matched config (GRP=2) was real and 2.6x SLOWER than ARM0 -- same log. This violated the S0 plausibility rule (every output non-zero). Realtime budget back to ~0.53x (CT=4 ARM=0 stands: 1.35-2.07x, nonzero, bit-exact); x2.6 to 79 GMAC/s remains. 'Shared-load binder' UNSUPPORTED (ARM3, ARM5 cut shared loads and got slower; ARM2 fewer ops/higher occ slower; ARM4 prefetch -7%): binder unidentified. 'KC truncation at CT8' note WRONG: KC=1920 nch=4 (196608 cells), not 240. Survives: S8 gate ARM5(H2) T=1 == q8_partial bit-exact 153/153 on real nonzero activations; swap measured-out result (F 11/16, decode 304 ms) is real. Default CT=2 ARM=0 regression green. Shipped engine untouched.

description: ARM=6 coalesced weight staging inside q8_prefill_h2 (per-warp 1 KB coalesced int4 load per 32 blocks into shared, per-lane read). Bit-exact vs ARM0 on all 8 shapes (max rel 0), nonzero outputs, 0 launch errors. Speed 2-3.5x SLOWER than ARM0 in the engine (embed 16.9 vs 29.8, w2 8.6 vs 32.0, w1 16.7 vs 29.3, conv 16.4 vs 27.7). The bench's 2.9x did not transfer: the bench reads x from global. Plausible cause (not measured): added shared stores/loads and warp syncs per 32 blocks. Discarded; binder still unidentified; uncoalesced weight loads removed from candidates for this kernel.

asi.hypothesis: coalesced weight staging (bench 2.9x) lifts the engine's H2 prefill
asi.result: No: bit-exact but 2-3.5x slower; the bench's effect does not transfer to a kernel that already stages x in shared memory.

description: Binder search, measured. Board facts: Nano GPU = 1 SM (not 2), ~904 MHz sustained after ~0.4 s DVFS ramp (warm vs cold harness within 2%: earlier rates valid), CT4 H2 kernel = 2 blocks/SM = 16 warps by the occupancy API. Measured ceilings (bench/peak_rates.cu): HFMA2 105.8 GMAC/s (45% of datasheet 236), FFMA 82, LDS 100.5 GB/s, engine chain shape with register operands 97 GMAC/s at 16 warps. SASS b-loop: 212 instr/iteration (64 LDS, 64 HFMA2, 16 PRMT, 16 HADD2, 8 LOP, 8 F2F, 3 LDG). ARM=8 clock64 profile (bit-exact vs ARM0): b-loops 72-81%, reductions 11-20%, staging ~7%; wave arithmetic reproduces measured times. ARM=7 ablations (control bit-exact): no global loads +15%, no shared reads +20-28%, both 1.8x -> TWO co-binders. Correction: first ABL8/26 used one register x for all positions (chains mergeable); with distinct per-position x (SASS 64 HFMA2) ABL26 = 1.8x not 2.2x. ABL4 confounded, ABL1 faults: unused. Plausibility gate tightened 236 -> 120 GMAC/s (measured ceiling).

asi.hypothesis: identify the q8_prefill_h2 stall binder
asi.result: Two co-binders (global-load latency and shared loads); each alone holds the kernel near 30 GMAC/s. With both deleted the kernel reaches ~54, still below the ~79 realtime needs.

description: Arms against the two co-binders, all bit-exact vs ARM0 (max rel 0, 8/8): ARM9 row blocking RB1/2/4 (RB1 = k-outer order +9% embed/w1, -7% w2; RB2/4 no gain despite 1/2-1/4 shared loads per MAC); ARM10 = RB2 + all global loads (weights AND scales) prefetched one iteration ahead over a flattened (row-group,b) space: +6-9% (embed 31.7, w2 35.5, w1 31.6, conv 31.4 vs 29.8/32.5/29.8/29.8). Best bit-exact arm, test-only, not adopted. Realtime assessment: needs ~79 GMAC/s; practical HFMA2 ceiling 106, engine chain shape 97 with no memory, ABL26 (all loads deleted) 54 -> 79 is above anything this kernel family has shown even with memory removed; budget at the best arm ~0.56x. Further progress needs a different formulation or less work (scope decisions). Fresh-build shipped path: regression 8/8 bit-exact, gates 6/7 streams (same as baseline), CHECKS OK, 0 spinners.

asi.hypothesis: fixing both co-binders (row blocking + cross-row prefetch) recovers the ablation's 1.8x
asi.result: Partly: +6-9% bit-exact. Realtime is out of reach for this kernel family.

description: CORRECTION: the encoder emits 12.5 backbone tokens per second of audio, not 25. The plan read lin_out's 4096-wide input as a 4-frame concat; the downsampler is three stride-2 convs on BOTH axes (4096 = 16 mel bins x 256 channels). Measured with HF get_audio_features: 13/63/125/375 embeddings for 1/5/10/30 s. Prefill = 18.4 GMAC per audio-second (was 43.2). T=12 (one 0.96 s chunk) runs at the same rate as T=24, bit-exact (CT4 29.7-32.5, ARM10 RB2 31.3-35.3 GMAC/s). Tokenizer 1.141 tokens/word -> 2.85-4.0 text tok/s at 2.5-3.5 words/s. Corrected budget: prefill 0.56-0.61 s + encoder ~0.06 s (estimate) + decode 0.31-0.44 s = ~0.93-1.11 s per audio-second -> ~0.9-1.07x realtime, BORDERLINE, not demonstrated (encoder unported, batched prefill not integrated, non-GEMM prefill unmeasured). Section 17's 'out of reach' withdrawn. Also fixed: engine README projector (LN + 768->2048 + GELU + 2048->2048, not 3x768->768) and encoder cost (per token at 12.5/s batched, not per mel frame at 100/s). Docs: plan section 18 + in-place fixes in plan s2/s3, README, engine README.

asi.hypothesis: the realtime budget's 25 tok/s token rate is right
asi.result: No: 12.5/s measured with HF. Requirement drops 2.3x; realtime moves from 0.53x to ~0.9-1.07x on paper.
